train_test_split shuffles by default and returns a training part and a test part (25% test by default).
replies.assert:
import inspect
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
assert inspect.signature(train_test_split).parameters['shuffle'].default is True
X = list(range(20))
tr, te = train_test_split(X, random_state=0)
assert len(tr) == 15 and len(te) == 5
assert sorted(tr + te) == X
assert tr != sorted(tr)

replies.reason: The same random_state gives the same shuffle and so the same split on every run.

replies.assert:
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
X = [[i] for i in range(8)]
y = list(range(8))
r = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.25, random_state=0)
assert len(r) == 4 and all(isinstance(p, list) for p in r)
Xtr, Xte, ytr, yte = r
assert len(Xtr) == len(ytr) == 6 and len(Xte) == len(yte) == 2
assert [x[0] for x in Xte] == yte
